name: shakespeare-plays

description.en: 60 characters from 28 of Shakespeare's plays (tragedies, comedies, romances and two histories), each of whom appears in only one play. Front: the character's name in English and in Swedish (where Swedish has an established form of its own, such as Ofelia, Jago or Botten, that form; otherwise the original name); back: the play, by its English and Swedish title, with a short note on who the character is. Characters whose name is in the play's title are left out. Built from the play texts (Project Gutenberg) and Wikidata, with the Swedish names checked against C. A. Hagberg's translation, and cross-checked against the Folger Shakespeare.
description.sv: 60 rollfigurer ur 28 av Shakespeares pjäser (tragedier, komedier, sagospel och två krönikespel), som var och en förekommer i bara en pjäs. Framsida: rollfigurens namn på engelska och svenska (den etablerade svenska formen där en sådan finns, som Ofelia, Jago eller Botten, annars originalnamnet); baksida: pjäsen med dess engelska och svenska titel och en kort anteckning om vem rollfiguren är. Rollfigurer vars namn står i pjäsens titel ingår inte. Uppgifterna kommer från pjästexterna (Project Gutenberg) och Wikidata. De svenska namnen har kontrollerats mot C. A. Hagbergs översättning och allt har jämförts med Folger Shakespeare.

Each quote is linked to the exact revision read. No list or selection was taken from it. The Swedish back notes are the compiler's translations of the Gutenberg cast-list lines; quality-control round 3 found that three of them (Thersites, Rosalind, Apemantus) matched the wording of the articles' cast lists, and these were reworded from the Gutenberg and Hagberg lines. The remaining overlaps are a few words of a literal translation of the same public-domain English line (titles such as "Kung av Skottland", "Hertig av Illyrien", "Kung av Sicilien"; kinship and "förälskad i" phrases such as "Lears yngsta dotter", "förälskad i Lysander", "förälskad i Fenton"; the twins' names), listed in method step 10.

method: Research, drafting and cross-checking were done by AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund's direction, with independent AI reviewers and machine checks (the builder's checks against live Wikidata and the app's SHACL/DCAT-AP validators). The cards have not yet been reviewed by a human subject expert.

The play texts: Project Gutenberg's Complete Works of William Shakespeare (eBook #100, updated 2025-08-24) was downloaded as plain text (query 1). The script split_plays.py (query 2) split it into its 38 plays using the table of contents (the six poem collections were set aside) and, for each play, extracted the Dramatis Personæ list (36 plays have one; King Richard the Second and The Two Noble Kinsmen have none) and every speech prefix (a line in capitals ending with a full stop).

Candidates: a list of 145 well-known leads and supporting roles (146 lines, Shylock twice; recorded verbatim with query 3) was drawn up by the compiler and run through where.py (query 3), which lists for each name every play whose Dramatis Personæ or speech prefixes name it, and every other play whose text merely mentions it. A name qualified only if exactly one play has it as a character. This removed, among others, Claudius (also in Julius Caesar), Edmund (King Lear and three histories), Emilia (four plays), Helena (All's Well and A Midsummer Night's Dream), Demetrius (three plays), Theseus and Hippolyta (also in The Two Noble Kinsmen), Portia (also in Julius Caesar), Antonio and Sebastian (several plays), Angelo and Mariana (two plays each), Valentine (three plays), Brutus (also in Coriolanus), Caius, Pompey, and Falstaff's company (Bardolph, Pistol, Nym, Mistress Quickly, Shallow).

Independent check against the Folger edition: fetch_folger.py (query 4) downloaded the character list of all 38 Folger plays (https://www.folgerdigitaltexts.org/<play>/charText/), and verify.py (query 5) required, for every card, that the Gutenberg check and the Folger check both give the card's play and no other (Folger's CamelCase ids such as DromioOfSyracuse were split into words; Folger lists Puck as Robin Goodfellow). This removed Petruchio, whom Folger also lists as a minor speaking character in Romeo and Juliet. The final 60 cards pass both checks; verify.json records the result for each.

Every other occurrence of a card's name in the other plays was read (query 6): all are mentions, not characters (e.g. "wise Laertes' son" for Ulysses in Titus Andronicus, "Sir Pandarus of Troy" in The Merry Wives of Windsor, the dead Cassius recalled in Antony and Cleopatra, "Lucio" in the list of guests Capulet invites in Romeo and Juliet), or, for Bottom and Sly, the ordinary English words.

Wikidata: queries 7 and 8 listed Shakespeare's works (P50 Q692) with their English and Swedish labels and the characters linked to them by P1441 (present in work); query 9 fetched the labels, aliases and sitelinks of the 28 plays; queries 10 and 11 looked for items for the characters that query 7 did not find (also through the plays' P674); query 12 fetched the labels, aliases and P1441 values of the character items found (47 of them are linked to the card's play and used; the item found for Aaron has no P1441 and is not used); query 13 the death date of Shakespeare. The English and Swedish titles on the backs are the Wikidata labels of the play items.

Swedish titles: each Swedish label was compared with the title of the play's Swedish Wikipedia article and its introduction (query 14) and with Swedish editions in LIBRIS (query 15). They agree for all 28 plays kept. LIBRIS found no edition with the exact titles Henrik V, Henrik VIII or Två ungherrar i Verona (Hagberg's titles are Konung Henrik den femte, Konung Henrik den åttonde and Två ungherrar från Verona); for these the Swedish Wikipedia article title, which is also the Wikidata label, was used. Pericles was left out because its Swedish title is not settled: Wikidata has "Perikles" (as the 1986 Swedish edition), Swedish Wikipedia "Pericles" (as the 1931 edition's "Sagospelet Pericles").

Swedish names: the front gives the name as Swedish writes it today. For most characters this is the original name. Where Swedish has a form of its own it was taken from a content source and checked against Swedish Wikipedia (query 16, counts of each variant; query 17, the quoted sentences): Ofelia (Wikidata sv label; Swedish Wikipedia 15 times, "Ophelia" 0), Jago (Hagberg; Swedish Wikipedia 32 times, "Iago" 0), Botten (Hagberg; Swedish Wikipedia 11 times; the Wikidata sv label is "Botten Vävare"), Benedict (Hagberg; Swedish Wikipedia 13 times, "Benedick" 0, but also "Benedikt" twice: the majority form, which is also Hagberg's, was kept, as for Rosalind/Rosalinda), Kardinal Wolsey (Hagberg's "Kardinal WOLSEY"; Swedish Wikipedia "kardinal Wolseys", the second sentence naming "kardinal Wolseys", chosen in quality-control round 1 because the first misplaces Wolsey's farewell speech; recorded as "|2" in svquotes.txt) and Christopher Sluger (Hagberg's "CHRISTOPHER SLUGER"; Swedish Wikipedia "fyllot Sluger" once, and "Sly" only in the link "[[Sly (opera)|Sly]]", which query 16 counts as 2, not for the character; adopted in quality-control round 2, the first draft had "Christopher Sly"). Hagberg's 1847–1851 translation (the classic Swedish one, read in Projekt Runeberg's edition, query 18) adapts other names too (Rosalinda, Orsinio, Jachimo, Jessika, Anna Page, Surkart for Dogberry), but the Swedish Wikipedia uses the original names for these (Swedish Wikipedia, following modern translations such as Göran O. Eriksson's), so the cards do too and the evidence records Hagberg's form (the Dogberry note also gives Surkart, which the article mentions). Other characters whose names Swedish translations render as Swedish words were left out (Sir Toby Belch, Hagberg's "Tobias Raap", Swedish Wikipedia's "Tobias Rap"; Sir Andrew Aguecheek, "Andreas Blek av Nosen"; Touchstone, "Proba"; Peter Quince, "Qvitten"/"Kvitten"): these forms come from particular translations and are not in Wikidata, and among translated names (as opposed to spellings) the deck keeps only Botten, which Hagberg, the Swedish Wikipedia and Wikidata's Swedish label all support, and Sluger, Hagberg's form, which the Swedish Wikipedia uses.

Every card's character was found in Hagberg's cast list ("Personer") of the same play (query 18; fetch_hagberg.py saved the cast-list pages, evidence_table.py found the line), which also confirms that the Swedish translation has the character in that play.

Back notes: each card has a short note on who the character is, written by the compiler from the character's description in the Gutenberg Dramatis Personæ (e.g. "BANQUO, General in the King's Army", "TYBALT, nephew to Lady Capulet"), translated into Swedish by the compiler and compared with Hagberg's description of the same character. Quality-control round 3 compared every Swedish note with the Swedish Wikipedia article on the play (CC BY-SA, verification only; script svoverlap.py, query 20): three notes matched its cast-list wording (Thersites "En vanskapt och hånfull grek", Rosalind "dotter till den äldre hertigen", Apemantus "vresig filosof") and were reworded from the Gutenberg and Hagberg lines ("En missbildad och grovkäftad grek", "Dotter till den landsförvisade hertigen", "En butter filosof"). The overlaps left are three or four words of a literal translation of the same English cast-list line, which any translation would share: "Kung av Skottland" (Duncan), "Lears yngsta dotter" (Cordelia), "förälskad i Lysander" (Hermia), "Hertig av Illyrien" (Orsino), "Kung av Sicilien" (Leontes), "dotter, förälskad i Fenton" (Anne Page), "de två ungherrarna" (Proteus, from the play's title) and the twins' names (Dromio). Five notes add a fact from the play text that the cast list does not give: Tybalt is Lady Capulet's (Fru Capulets) brother's son ("Tybalt, my cousin! O my brother’s child!", Act III, Scene 1; Hagberg's "systerson" is not followed); Wolsey, who has no description in the cast list, is the King's favourite who falls from power (Act III, Scene 2: "Farewell? A long farewell to all my greatness!"); Laertes is Ophelia's brother and Ophelia his sister (both are Polonius's children in the cast list); Lucio is Claudio's friend (he goes to Isabella on Claudio's behalf; Swedish Wikipedia: "Claudios vän Lucio"); Bottom's first name Nick ("Nick Bottom, the weaver" in Act I, Scene 2). English forms of address in the notes are translated as "Fru" (Mistress Page "Fru Page", Lady Capulet "Fru Capulet"; quality-control round 5), since Swedish Wikipedia gives no Swedish form for Lady Capulet and Hagberg's "grefvinnan" is a 19th-century rank not in the English. Kinship words were translated neutrally where English does not say which side: nephew is "nevö" (Benvolio), niece "niece" (Beatrice: the play never says whose daughter she is, so Hagberg's "brorsdotter" is not followed), uncle "onkel".

Machine checks: for every card the builder checks against live Wikidata the English and Swedish labels of the play item (the back). For the 47 cards whose character has a Wikidata item linked to the play, it also checks that the item's P1441 (present in work) includes the play, and the item's English label or alias equal to the front, and its Swedish label (or multilingual label) where it equals the Swedish front. Labels not checked, and why: King Duncan (Q15698348, label "King Duncan", no alias "Duncan"), Botten (sv label "Botten Vävare"), Pandarus (sv label "Pandaros", the Homeric form, on an item that is also the figure of the Iliad), and characters with no Swedish label. The deck was then validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (scripts/validate_sources.ts).
selection: 60 characters from 28 plays: the tragedies Hamlet, Macbeth, Othello, Romeo and Juliet, King Lear, Julius Caesar, Antony and Cleopatra, Coriolanus, Titus Andronicus, Timon of Athens and Troilus and Cressida; the comedies A Midsummer Night's Dream, The Merchant of Venice, Twelfth Night, Much Ado About Nothing, As You Like It, The Taming of the Shrew, Measure for Measure, All's Well That Ends Well, The Comedy of Errors, The Merry Wives of Windsor, Love's Labour's Lost and The Two Gentlemen of Verona; the romances The Tempest, The Winter's Tale and Cymbeline; and the histories Henry V and Henry VIII. Between one and five characters per play, more for the most read plays. A character is included only if (1) exactly one of the 38 plays in the Gutenberg Complete Works has a character of that name, in its cast list or speech prefixes, and the Folger edition agrees; (2) the name is not in the play's title (so no Hamlet, Macbeth, Lady Macbeth, Romeo, Juliet, Lear, Othello, Julius Caesar, Antony, Cleopatra, Coriolanus, Cymbeline, Titus, Troilus, Cressida or Timon; Shylock is kept, since the title is The Merchant of Venice); (3) the character is a lead or a well-known supporting role; (4) the name has one form in current Swedish writing, taken to be the form the Swedish Wikipedia article on the play uses: a Swedish form of its own (Ofelia, Jago, Botten, Benedict, Kardinal Wolsey, Christopher Sluger) or the original name; a form found only in Hagberg's 19th-century translation (Rosalinda, Surkart for Dogberry) does not count, and the back note mentions it where the article does. Left out: characters who recur in several plays (Falstaff, Mistress Quickly, Bardolph, Pistol, Nym, Shallow) or share a name with a character of another play (see the method); the history plays King John, Richard II, Richard III and Henry IV and VI, whose Swedish titles are not settled (Wikidata has Rickard II and Rikard III, Swedish Wikipedia Richard II, Richard III and Kung John against Wikidata's Kung Johan; Henry IV, Part 2 has no Swedish label) and whose figures often recur; Pericles, whose Swedish title is not settled (Perikles or Pericles); The Two Noble Kinsmen (co-written with John Fletcher, not in the First Folio, and with no Swedish title of its own); Edward III, which the Gutenberg Complete Works does not include. Characters whose speech prefix or cast-list name is not their name (Feste is "Clown" in the Gutenberg cast list) or who never appear on stage (Sycorax, Yorick) were also left out. Isabella (Measure for Measure) was left out because Hagberg's Swedish translation calls the Queen of France in Henry V Isabella as well.

queries.query:
"""Split Project Gutenberg eBook #100 (pg100.txt) into its plays and index each
play's Dramatis Personae and speech prefixes. Writes plays.json."""
import json, re
from pathlib import Path

D = Path(__file__).parent
text = (D / "pg100.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
body = text.split("*** START OF THE PROJECT GUTENBERG EBOOK")[1].split("*** END OF THE PROJECT GUTENBERG EBOOK")[0]
lines = body.splitlines()

# The contents list (indented titles), in order.
start = next(i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l.strip() == "Contents")
titles = []
for l in lines[start + 1:]:
    if not l.strip():
        if titles:
            break
        continue
    titles.append(l.strip())

# Each work begins at the first line equal to its title after the contents.
pos = start + len(titles) + 2
starts = []
for t in titles:
    i = next(j for j in range(pos, len(lines)) if lines[j].strip() == t)
    starts.append(i)
    pos = i + 1
starts.append(len(lines))

POEMS = {"THE SONNETS", "A LOVER’S COMPLAINT", "THE PASSIONATE PILGRIM", "THE PHOENIX AND THE TURTLE",
         "THE RAPE OF LUCRECE", "VENUS AND ADONIS"}
plays = {}
for t, a, b in zip(titles, starts, starts[1:]):
    if t in POEMS:
        continue
    seg = lines[a:b]
    # Dramatis Personae block: from the heading to the first "ACT I"/"INDUCTION"/"PROLOGUE" heading.
    dp_start = next((k for k, l in enumerate(seg) if l.strip().lower().startswith("dramatis person")), None)
    dp = []
    if dp_start is not None:
        for l in seg[dp_start + 1:]:
            s = l.strip()
            if re.match(r"^(ACT I\b|INDUCTION|PROLOGUE|THE PROLOGUE|ACT 1)", s):
                break
            if s:
                dp.append(s)
    prefixes = sorted({l.strip()[:-1] for l in seg if re.match(r"^[A-Z][A-Z’' .,-]+\.$", l.strip())
                       and not re.match(r"^(ACT|SCENE|EPILOGUE|PROLOGUE|INDUCTION)\b", l.strip())})
    plays[t] = {"lines": [a, b], "dramatisPersonae": dp, "speechPrefixes": prefixes, "text": "\n".join(seg)}

(D / "plays.json").write_text(json.dumps(plays, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
for t, p in plays.items():
    print(f"{t}: {len(p['dramatisPersonae'])} DP lines, {len(p['speechPrefixes'])} prefixes")

queries.purpose: 3. For each candidate name (candidates.txt, 145 names; its contents are recorded as query 3a below), the plays that have it as a character and the plays that only mention it (python3 where.py)
queries.query:
"""For each name given on the command line (or in candidates.txt), list the plays of
Gutenberg #100 whose Dramatis Personae or speech prefixes name it, and every play whose
text mentions it (whole word, case-insensitive), with counts."""
import json, re, sys
from pathlib import Path

D = Path(__file__).parent
plays = json.loads((D / "plays.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
names = sys.argv[1:] or [l.strip() for l in (D / "candidates.txt").read_text().splitlines() if l.strip()]
short = lambda t: re.sub(r"^(THE TRAGEDY OF |THE LIFE OF |THE LIFE AND DEATH OF )", "", t)
for n in names:
    pat = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z])" + re.escape(n) + r"(?![a-z])", re.I)
    role, mention = [], []
    for t, p in plays.items():
        inrole = any(pat.search(x) for x in p["dramatisPersonae"]) or any(pat.search(x) for x in p["speechPrefixes"])
        c = len(pat.findall(p["text"]))
        if inrole:
            role.append(f"{short(t)}({c})")
        elif c:
            mention.append(f"{short(t)}({c})")
    flag = "OK " if len(role) == 1 else "XX "
    print(f"{flag}{n}: ROLE {role}  MENTION {mention}")

"""Extract, from the fetched sv.wikipedia wikitext, the n-th sentence or list line naming a word (wiki markup
stripped to plain text as displayed; n = 1 unless given). Spec: svquotes.txt 'card|article|word[|n]'.
Writes svquotes.json."""
import json, re
from pathlib import Path

H = Path(__file__).parent
D = H / "svwiki"

def plain(s):
    s = re.sub(r"(?s)<ref[^>]*/>|<ref.*?</ref>", "", s)
    s = re.sub(r"\[\[(?:[^|\]]*\|)?([^\]]*)\]\]", r"\1", s)
    s = re.sub(r"'''?", "", s)
    return s

out = {}
for line in (H / "svquotes.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    if not line.strip():
        continue
    cid, art, word, *n = line.split("|")
    n = int(n[0]) if n else 1
    a = json.loads((D / f"{art}.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    text = plain(a["content"])
    pieces = re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+|\n", text)
    hits = [p.strip() for p in pieces if re.search(r"(?<![\wåäö])" + re.escape(word) + r"(?![a-zåäö])", p)]
    hit = hits[n - 1] if len(hits) >= n else None
    out[cid] = {"article": a["title"], "revid": a["revid"], "word": word, "n": n, "quote": hit}
    print(cid, a["revid"], "::", hit)
(H / "svquotes.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")

The reviewer's own scan of the Folger lists found every character in exactly one play, the play on the card's back; the Wikidata labels of all 28 plays agree with the backs; the builder's 235 checks pass. Two warnings (the Swedish Bottom note used the English name; the Dromio evidence said 39 plays) and three suggestions. Three findings were fixed and two suggestions declined.

findings.issue: The Swedish Wikipedia sentence quoted to show the form "kardinal Wolsey" puts Wolsey's speech after his fall in act five; the speech ("Farewell? A long farewell to all my greatness!") is in Act III, Scene 2.
findings.resolution: Confirmed in the Gutenberg text (the speech follows the heading "SCENE II. Ante-chamber to the King’s apartment." under ACT III). The quote was replaced by another sentence of the same revision that shows the form without the error: "Pjäsen börjar med att Buckingham … beklagar sig över kardinal Wolseys hänsynslösa och övermodiga styre."

findings.issue: Suggests the Swedish note "Leonatos brorsdotter." (Hagberg's wording) instead of "Leonatos niece.", taking Beatrice to be the daughter of Leonato's brother Antonio.
findings.resolution: Rejected. The play never says whose daughter Beatrice is: the cast list says only "Niece to Leonato", and in Act V, Scene 1 Leonato says "My brother hath a daughter, / Almost the copy of my child that’s dead", a daughter who is not Beatrice (she turns out to be Hero), so Beatrice is not shown to be Antonio's daughter. "Brorsdotter" would add a claim the text does not make; "niece" is a Swedish word (SAOL) and keeps the English neutrality, as method step 10 records.

findings.issue: Optionally mention that some modern editions (Oxford, RSC) call her "Innogen".
findings.resolution: Declined. The card is correct, and all the deck's sources (Gutenberg, Folger, Hagberg, Wikidata Q6005653, which has no alias "Innogen", checked 2026-10-04) use "Imogen"; adding the variant would need a further source for the editions that use it, for a fact that is not needed to answer the card.
